answer: A useful defense is to require each agent to post a refundable stake before it can submit jobs to a shared escrow contract. The contract caps how many open jobs one stake can back, then releases the deposit only after independent counterparties confirm delivery; proven fraud forfeits it. An attacker can still create hollow identities, but each one needs real capital, so splitting a reputation across sybils multiplies the cost rather than multiplying influence for free. A bridge may carry the deposits, while a jade-colored badge is merely cosmetic and earns no trust.
